audit.whatIsWrong: THE decisive interaction was inverted. wants.you[1], spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text, mid and late all told you to save Dark Procession to 'trap her E hookshot'. Hookshot pulls Camille TO A WALL. Dark Procession creates terrain. The wall you cast to cage her is the anchor she needs to leap on top of you or out of your all-in.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing' (E, 16/15/14/13/12s, 800 range). Yorick's W 'summons a destructible wall'. The page repeated the wrong instruction in five places and never once warned that your own W arms her engage — the same shape of error the mirror slice found on Akshan's Heroic Swing.
audit.corrected: Every wall line now says cage her exit, never her approach, and states that terrain — including your own — is a Hookshot anchor. Duelling advice moved to open lane away from terrain.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with their own why-text. win[2]/phases[2].side read 'Camille' while whys[2] and spikes[0].text both call level 3 even; win[3] read 'Skill' while whys[3] says Camille retakes levels 4-5; win[4] read 'Camille' while whys[4] calls level 6 a skill wash; win[5] read 'Skill' while whys[5] says Camille favours the first-item spike.
audit.why: The packet levelChart (Camille, Camille, Skill, Camille, Skill, Camille, Camille) agrees with the prose on all four rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 2-5 aligned to the packet across both layers as one atomic pair-matched group, with ratings brought along.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appeared in any spike, despite Hookshot being named as the tracked cooldown in nine separate fields.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16s at rank 1 and The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s. Those are the two numbers the whole lane is played around.
audit.corrected: mid now carries Hookshot's 16s and spikes[1].text the Ultimatum's 140s.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet suspectNames flags 'Hextech Ultimatum' in spikes[1].text. The ability's real name carries the article.
audit.why: Riot's name is 'The Hextech Ultimatum'. It also does not 'lock you in a zone with no escape' as a standalone effect — she dashes to a target champion and anchors them to the area.
audit.corrected: Full name used and the anchor described as what it is.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds appeared only in a generic itemization line; nothing said when it matters or why.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule 'needs-antiheal': Tactical Sweep heals Camille off enemies caught in its outer half (15/14/13/12/11s), which is exactly the extended trade Yorick's ghouls force. The second flagged rule, 'autoreset-burst-tell', applies too: Precision Protocol is an auto-attack reset whose delayed second cast hits much harder as true damage, so the wind-up between her two attacks is the tell.
audit.corrected: early now names the delayed second hit, the outer-half heal, and buying Grievous Wounds early; dosFull[2].d states that true damage ignores the armour the page told you to stack.

edits.before: Camille runs levels 1-2 — her Q Precision Protocol true-damage proc and W heal beat your melee trades, and her passive shield eats your poke. Give ground, soak XP with ghouls, and don't stand where her E hookshot can pin you to a wall.
edits.after: Camille runs levels 1-2 — Precision Protocol's delayed second hit lands as true damage and Tactical Sweep's outer half heals her, while Adaptive Defenses shields against your damage type. Buy Grievous Wounds early and fight away from walls.

edits.before: Level 3 is your even beat — bait out her E, then land E Mourning Mist and Q while she has no mobility. She reasserts from 4, and at 6 Hextech Ultimatum locks you down for a full combo, so hold Cage strictly for her engage.
edits.after: Level 3 is your even beat — bait Hookshot (16s), then land Mourning Mist and Q while she has no mobility. She reasserts from 4, and at 6 The Hextech Ultimatum anchors you for a full combo, so cage her exit, never her approach.

edits.before: Camille favours the dive-and-pick game, so beat her on the map: split-push with Maiden, take towers when she rotates, and only take a sidelane duel with W Cage up to trap her E and stop her escaping the loss.
edits.after: Camille favours the dive-and-pick game, so beat her on the map: split-push with Maiden, take towers when she rotates, and duel her away from terrain in the side lane — every wall is a Hookshot anchor for her.

edits.before: Camille spikes at 6 — Hextech Ultimatum locks you in a zone with no escape and lets her execute her full Q-W-E combo on you. Save W Cage to answer her E engage and never fight when her hookshot is up.
edits.after: Camille spikes at 6 — The Hextech Ultimatum (140s) dashes to you and anchors you there for her full combo. Never wall her in: Dark Procession is terrain, and Hookshot pulls to walls, so your cage becomes her engage.

edits.before: The lock stays Camille but late is your split window — she's a dive assassin, you're a wave-eating split-pusher. Shove with Maiden, take side towers, and only 1v1 her with Cage ready to trap her E and deny the reset.
edits.after: The lock stays Camille but late is your split window — she's a dive assassin, you're a wave-eating split-pusher. Shove with Maiden, take side towers, and fight her in open lane where she has no wall left to Hookshot off.

edits.before: W Cage to trap her E hookshot or R zone
edits.after: Cage her exit — a wall feeds her Hookshot

edits.before: E hookshot mobility to stick and reposition
edits.after: Hookshot off any wall to engage or escape

edits.before: Camille wastes Hookshot — commit the full pattern immediately.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Every wall is a Hookshot anchor — and your own W builds one.

notes: The single most important correction in this file: the page told you five separate times to use Dark Procession to trap Camille's Hookshot, when Hookshot's entire mechanic is pulling to a wall. Casting W to cage her hands her the terrain. If only some of these edits apply, the ones that matter are spikes[1].text, wants.you[1] and dontsFull[1].d. Unverified and therefore not written: whether Camille is untargetable during The Hextech Ultimatum's dash (the kit file flags untargetable and channel, but Riot's description mentions neither), and whether Mist Walkers can body-block the Hookshot leap.
